verses.verse:
त्रिरुक्तः स्वरसंघातः तृधायीति निगद्यते।
तानावसाने संयोज्यो मुख्यान्तश्च गुणान्वितः।१४२।
verses.text: A cluster of notes said three times is called tṛdhāyī (tihāī); it is to be joined at the end of a tāna, should end on the main [note], and must have some quality.

commentary.text: That is, a group of notes used three times in a row is called a tihāī (a phrase played three times to land on sam); but the last note of that group should be the main sam note of the rāga, and the group must have a quality made by laya or a quality made by rāga. By quality made by laya is meant layakārī (rhythmic play), and by quality made by rāga is meant the rāga-identifying svara saṅgati (companionship of notes).

The tihāī belongs to tāla; it arises in the bols of the tabla. Most commonly 'dhā' is used at its end, e.g. - 'tiṭ dhā tiṭ dhā tiṭ dhā' and so on. These bols contain three dhās, so its correct name is (tridhāyī), whose corrupted form is known as (tihāī). If the sam is likened to a temple, we liken the tihāīs to the three steps that lead into the temple. Just as the third dhā comes to rest on the sam, so the third step comes to rest in the temple. Now the many kinds of tihāī are considered.
